conviction_note: Sum of findings is +1.3; I nudge to +1.5 because the two prints in the baseline that are genuinely earnings (2026-03-11 +4.17%, 2026-06-03/04 +5.13%) were both positive even while the stock fell 22% YTD, i.e. DSGX has been beating into a derating tape and the damage happens between prints, not on them; the real earnings move for this name is ~5-6%, not the 2.21% the sweep flagged as unusable.

findings.finding: The entire CBP IEEPA-refund filing wave landed inside Descartes' May-July quarter -- CAPE Phase 1 deployed 2026-04-20, Phase 2 on 2026-06-29, Phase 3 late July -- against ~53 million entries and ~330,000 importers, and Descartes sells the batch Post-Summary-Correction automation and duty-recovery service that brokers need to work those entries at scale, so the customs-transaction line likely beat the $169.0m Q2 baseline by more than its usual margin.
findings.why_not_priced: The wire frame on DSGX is that the February 2026 Supreme Court strike-down of IEEPA tariffs removes trade complexity and therefore demand -- that is the frame that took the stock 30% off its high and left puts bid. If the market had worked through the mechanics it would see the opposite for this one quarter: unwinding $166bn of duties across 53m entries is itself a one-time filing surge, and it fell precisely in the May-July window. With only two published estimates there is no model that carries a PSC-volume line, and Descartes' guidance construct (a $169.0m contracted 'baseline' plus whatever transactional volume arrives) means this shows up exactly in the beat-over-baseline, which is the number the stock trades on.
findings.independence: Descartes' own product page for the refund wave describes automating 'every step of the PSC lifecycle' and 'batch PSC filing, allowing thousands of entries to be processed simultaneously' (https://www.descartes.com/resources/knowledge-center/tariff-refunds-ieepa-tariffs, undated page), and its 2026-04-22 news item sizes the pool at '$166 billion and more than 330,000 importers' (https://www.descartes.com/resources/news/tariff-refund-portal-launch-creates-new-cost-recovery-path-ecommerce-sellers). Caveat I will not hide: the CAPE declaration itself is a CSV upload to the ACE portal, not an ABI transaction, so Descartes' monetisation is via the PSC/duty-recovery work around it rather than the declaration -- that is why the low end of my band is below zero.

findings.finding: Descartes' own monthly container data for the quarter it is about to report: May 2026 2,428,758 TEU (+11.5% YoY), June 2,400,627 (+8.2% YoY), July 2,508,310 (-4.3% YoY) -- about +4.6% YoY for the May-July quarter -- and the report published this morning (2026-09-10) puts August at 2,603,709 TEU, +3.8% MoM, +3.3% YoY, the third-highest month on record.
findings.why_not_priced: Genuinely two-sided and that is why I size it small: July was the first negative YoY month of 2026 and it is the last month of the reporting quarter, which argues the volume-linked line decelerated hard through the quarter; but the quarter was still +4.6% YoY and the exit rate re-accelerated to a near-record August. If the market had read Descartes' own series rather than the generic 'soft freight' headline, the stock would not be 5.25% lower over five sessions into a print whose volume backdrop is a record-adjacent August. Nobody aggregates a company's own free monthly dataset as a nowcast of its own quarter.
findings.independence: The August figure is separately reported by IT Supply Chain, dated 2026-09-10, with the same 2,603,709 TEU and 'third-highest on record' framing (https://itsupplychain.com/august-u-s-containerized-imports-reach-third-highest-level-on-record-amid-persistent-trade-risk/). Note this is the same underlying Descartes dataset -- a second outlet, not a second source. The May and June months come from separate Descartes releases (https://www.descartes.com/resources/knowledge-center/global-shipping-report-june-2026-container-imports-stabilize).

findings.finding: Descartes deployed roughly $250m of cash on four weeks of M&A around quarter-end -- Drivin $30m on 2026-07-06 (in-quarter), Tai $100m on 2026-08-24 and Extensiv $120m on 2026-09-01 (both post-quarter, eight days apart) -- and Extensiv is a distressed-timeline asset: its $80m Runway Growth senior secured term loan matured 2026-06-30, 63 days before the sale, and the price is roughly 1.2-2.4x revenue against Descartes' own 46% adjusted-EBITDA-margin base.
findings.why_not_priced: The announcements are public and the tape sold both of them (-1.21% on 24 Aug, -2.41% on 1 Sep in the sealed baseline), so the fact of the deals is priced. What is not priced is the size: neither press release discloses revenue, EBITDA or accretion, so nothing in consensus -- two estimates -- carries a number. Descartes will for the first time calibrate a Q3 baseline that includes them on this call, and its Q2 baseline construct was $169.0m revenue / $102.5m opex / $66.5m calibration = 39%. If the incremental revenue arrives at anything like the margin implied by a 1.2-2.4x revenue price on a company whose lender's clock had run out, the headline baseline-revenue jump comes with a visible step down in that 39%. If the market had done this arithmetic the skew would be steeper than 4.63 vol points and the deals would have drawn sell-side notes quantifying the dilution; they drew none.
findings.independence: Runway Growth Finance's schedule of investments prices the 3PL Central/Extensiv loan at SOFR+7.00% with a 9.00% floor and a 2026-06-30 maturity, well wide of its other software credits (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001653384/000119312526211877/rway-20260331.htm, 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-03-31, filed 2026-05-07). A separate analysis dated 2026-09-01 reaches the 1.2x-revenue conclusion (https://brendonbeebe.substack.com/p/what-happened-to-extensiv-the-company) -- but I treat that substack and the RWAY loan terms as one cluster, because the substack's argument is built on the same loan. The independent leg is Extensiv's own LinkedIn page, self-declared 201-500 employees with 153 profiles visible, which caps plausible revenue well below the $90-100m the substack extrapolates and is why my band stays wide (https://www.linkedin.com/company/goextensiv).

findings.finding: WiseTech Global, the closest listed comparable, guided FY27 CargoWise revenue growth of approximately 12-20% at its 2026-08-25 results, an acceleration from the 11% CargoWise growth it just delivered, and reported that its own acquisition (e2open) cut underlying EBITDA margin by 7 points to 46%.
findings.why_not_priced: An ASX result reported in Australian hours two weeks ago is not in US wire copy on DSGX, and DSGX has no shared analyst coverage with WTC. The demand read is positive -- the nearest peer is guiding logistics-software growth up, not down, which contradicts the 'soft freight demand' frame priced into DSGX. If the read-across had been made, DSGX would not have fallen 5.25% over the last five sessions. I size it small because WiseTech's own stock fell 6% on that guide, so the market's reading of the same disclosure was negative, and because the margin half of it points the same way as finding 3 rather than against it.
findings.independence: Same event, second outlet, with the AUD 1.3959bn revenue and 46% margin figures: https://kalkine.com.au/news/announcements/wisetech-global-releases-fy26-results-investor-presentation-for-year-ended-30-june-2026 . Not an independent fact.

A Q3 FY2027 baseline revenue/calibration figure anywhere ahead of the call (the Q1 MD&A gives only Q2: $169.0m revenue, $102.5m opex, $66.5m calibration)
Extensiv layoff, churn, outage or customer-complaint evidence -- no layoff tracker entry, no support-forum thread, no product-status incident found
Runway Growth's June-2026 10-Q line for the Extensiv loan (file exceeds the fetch size limit); the loan was never on non-accrual so there is no distress mark to point to

A wording change in the '5% to 7% of aggregate annualized recurring services revenues' attrition sentence -- present in the Q1 FY27 MD&A, could not locate the comparable sentence in the FY2026 annual MD&A to test whether the range widened
Descartes' careers page (404) and any job-posting count that would show a team added or deleted
Any peer pre-announcement, negative or positive, in the last two weeks (SPS Commerce, Manhattan Associates, C.H. Robinson, Expeditors -- nothing in the window)
Any 6-K between 2026-06-12 and 2026-08-24 other than the three acquisition releases -- the stream is clean, no quiet filing
baseline_tension: My net is mildly positive and therefore cuts against the baseline's positive 4.63-point put skew, the 2.97 put/call open interest ratio and the -5.25% five-day run-in -- though the option chain is unusable at an 81%-of-mid spread, and the two entries in the reaction history that are actually earnings prints (+4.17% and +5.13%) both went the way I am leaning even as the stock derated 22% year-to-date.
